newsitem.title: CHILE: Peru's Quellaveco seen at 200,000 tns/yr copper.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Quellaveco seen at 200,000 tns/yr copper.

text.p: Peruvian Quellaveco copper project is expected to produce 200,000 tonnes of fine copper in concentrates per year over its lifespan, said Minorco director Josef Oppenheimer.
He said the mine, in southern Peru, will cost around $800 million to build.
The project's feasibility study should be completed by January and the mine is likely to come on onstream in the year 2000 at the earliest, Oppenheimer told reporters.
Minorco owns Chile's Mantos Blancos, which itself controls Quellaveco.

Quellaveco has mining reserves of 500 million tonnes with an average ore grade of 0.8 percent. The ore grade starts out at about one percent in the project's early stages and later falls to 0.65 percent, said Oppenheimer.
